$comment: The presign REQUEST body. The corpus covered presign RESPONSES from the start and never the request, so a host could ask for the wrong thing — or for nothing — and stay green through every gate. One host shipped an empty object and the route's schema rejected it; the other shipped the deprecated alias and got the right bytes only because the orders it was tried on happened to carry no glb artifact.
deprecatedAliasNote: 'glb' also names a REAL artifact format, so as a whole-bundle request it is ambiguous: the platform looks up a glb artifact first and only falls through to the archive when the order has none. A host asking this way is reading the server's data, not stating its intent, and gets a mesh where it expected a zip.
bodyNote: The route validates against a schema, so an empty object is a 400 rather than a default meaning 'the usual one'. There is no default.

formatVectors.note: a real artifact format; accepted, but it asks for the MESH
the archive's file extension is not its format token
